cards.a: IGMP snooping is a Layer 2 switch feature that inspects IGMP membership messages and builds per-group forwarding tables so multicast is sent only out ports that have members instead of flooding the whole VLAN.

cards.q: Why does a switch need IGMP snooping?
cards.a: Without snooping the switch floods multicast like broadcast to every port, wasting bandwidth and CPU; snooping limits forwarding to only the ports that reported membership.
An mrouter port is the switch port facing the multicast router or querier; group traffic is forwarded out member ports plus the mrouter port so the router continues to see the group.

cards.q: How does a switch learn which ports are group members?
cards.a: It snoops or listens to IGMP reports sent by hosts on the VLAN and records each reporting port as a member of that group in its forwarding table.

cards.q: What is the difference between IGMP snooping and IGMP proxying?
cards.a: IGMP snooping inspects reports and builds L2 per-port forwarding tables while passing queries through, whereas IGMP proxying terminates and regenerates queries at Layer 3, summarizing membership like a router.

cards.q: What is the switch querier feature?
cards.a: The switch querier lets a switch act as the IGMP querier for a VLAN when no multicast router is present, so membership processing continues without a router.

cards.q: Is IGMP snooping enabled by default on Cisco switches?
cards.a: Yes, IGMP snooping is enabled by default on most Cisco switches, and it can be controlled per VLAN with commands such as ip igmp snooping vlan 10.

cards.q: Which commands verify IGMP snooping state?
cards.a: show ip igmp snooping, show ip igmp snooping groups, show ip igmp snooping mrouter, and show mac address-table multicast.

cards.q: Multicast is being flooded to all ports despite snooping; what is likely wrong?
cards.a: IGMP snooping is probably disabled on the VLAN, or the mrouter port is not correctly learned, so the switch has no group-to-port table; check show ip igmp snooping.

cards.q: What is the key exam distinction between IGMP and IGMP snooping?
cards.a: IGMP is the host-to-router (Layer 3) membership protocol, while IGMP snooping is a switch Layer 2 feature that peeks at IGMP messages to restrict flooding.

cards.q: What is the IGMP snooping quick-review summary?
cards.a: IGMP snooping is a Layer 2 switch feature, on by default, that snoops IGMP reports to build per-group member-port tables and forwards multicast only to member ports plus the mrouter port, passing queries through and optionally using a switch querier.
